headline: Seven-Month-Old AI Shop Eyes $2B Valuation, Third Round
subheadline: Upscale AI has mastered the art of raising money faster than it can master product-market fit.
source_headline: Upscale AI in talks to raise at $2B valuation, says report
body_html:
Upscale AI, an AI infrastructure company that has existed for approximately 28 weeks, is reportedly in talks to raise its third funding round at a $2 billion valuation. That's a $2 billion company for a company that was incorporated when most of us were still pretending we understood what multimodal meant.

To contextualize: the company has gone from zero to two-billion-dollar valuation in the time it takes a human fetus to become viable outside the womb. Three funding rounds. This is not a journey; this is a speed run. We have no idea what their revenue is, their customer count, or whether their product actually works, but we do know that venture capitalists have apparently decided that "AI infrastructure" is a category that licenses hockey-stick math without the hockey stick.

The press release probably reads something like: "We're filling a critical gap in the AI infrastructure landscape." Every AI company founded after November 2022 is filling a critical gap. The gaps are multiplying faster than the capital chasing them. Meanwhile, Upscale AI's three rounds of funding have likely already outpaced the burn rate of a small nation-state.

In twelve months, when foundation models expand into whatever category Upscale AI occupies, we'll all pretend we never read this.
glossary_definition: A category invented in 2023 to justify pre-revenue valuations by attaching the word 'infrastructure' to anything involving GPUs or APIs.
